verses.text: On the tenth day of the first month, in the twenty-fifth year of our exile, fourteen years after the city fell, on that very day the LORD's power came on me, and he took me there.
In visions from God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain. On the south side of it were some buildings that looked like a city.
He took me there, and I saw a man who looked like bronze. He was standing in the gateway, holding a linen cord and a measuring rod.

The man said to me, "Son of man, look carefully, listen closely, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, because that is why you have been brought here. Tell the people of Israel everything you see."

I saw a wall all the way around the outside of the temple area. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six cubits long, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the wall. It was one rod thick and one rod high.
Then he went to the gate facing east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate. It was one rod deep, and so was the other threshold.
Each guardroom was one rod long and one rod wide. The walls between the guardrooms were five cubits thick. The threshold of the gate next to the porch facing the temple was one rod deep.
He also measured the porch of the gateway facing the temple. It was one rod deep.
Then he measured the porch of the gateway. It was eight cubits deep, and its side pillars were two cubits thick. The porch of the gateway faced the temple.
Inside the east gate were three guardrooms on each side. All three had the same measurements, and the side pillars on each side had the same measurements.
He measured the width of the entrance of the gateway. It was ten cubits, and the length of the gateway was thirteen cubits.
In front of each guardroom was a low wall one cubit high, on each side. The guardrooms were six cubits square on each side.
He measured the gateway from the back wall of one guardroom to the back wall of the opposite one. It was twenty-five cubits from one doorway to the opposite doorway.
He measured the side pillars as sixty cubits, up to the courtyard around the gateway.
From the front of the entrance of the gateway to the far end of its porch was fifty cubits.
The guardrooms and their side pillars inside the gateway had narrow windows all around, and so did the porch. The windows all faced inward. The side pillars were decorated with palm trees.
Then he brought me into the outer courtyard. I saw rooms and a pavement built all around the courtyard. There were thirty rooms facing the pavement.
The pavement ran alongside the gateways, as long as the gateways were deep. This was the lower pavement.
Then he measured the distance from the inside of the lower gateway to the outside of the inner courtyard. It was one hundred cubits on the east side and on the north side.
Then he measured the length and width of the gate facing north, leading into the outer courtyard.
Its guardrooms, three on each side, its side pillars, and its porch had the same measurements as those of the first gateway. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, its porch, and its palm tree decorations had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, with its porch opposite them.
There was a gate to the inner courtyard opposite the north gate, just as there was on the east. He measured from one gate to the opposite gate. It was one hundred cubits.
Then he led me to the south side, and I saw a gate facing south. He measured its side pillars and its porch, and they had the same measurements as the others.
The gateway and its porch had narrow windows all around, like the other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Seven steps led up to it, with its porch opposite them. Its side pillars were decorated with palm trees, one on each side.
The inner courtyard also had a gate facing south. He measured from this gate to the outer gate on the south side. It was one hundred cubits.
Then he brought me into the inner courtyard through the south gate. He measured the south gate, and it had the same measurements as the others.
Its guardrooms, its side pillars, and its porch had the same measurements as the others. The gateway and its porch had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
The porches of the gateways around the inner courtyard were twenty-five cubits wide and five cubits deep.
Its porch faced the outer courtyard. Its side pillars were decorated with palm trees, and eight steps led up to it.
Then he brought me into the inner courtyard on the east side. He measured the gateway, and it had the same measurements as the others.
Its guardrooms, its side pillars, and its porch had the same measurements as the others. The gateway and its porch had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its porch faced the outer courtyard. Its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side, and eight steps led up to it.
Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it. It had the same measurements as the others,
as did its guardrooms, its side pillars, and its porch. It had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its side pillars faced the outer courtyard. They were decorated with palm trees on each side, and eight steps led up to it.
There was a room with a doorway by the side pillars of each inner gateway. This is where the burnt offerings were washed.
In the porch of the gateway were two tables on each side, where the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were slaughtered.
Outside, by the steps at the entrance of the north gateway, were two tables, and on the other side of the gateway's porch were two more tables.
So there were four tables on one side of the gateway and four on the other, eight tables in all, where the sacrifices were slaughtered.

There were also four tables of cut stone for the burnt offerings. Each was a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and one cubit high. On them were placed the tools used to slaughter the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices.
Hooks a handbreadth long were fastened all around the inside walls. The meat of the offerings was placed on the tables.
Outside the inner gate, in the inner courtyard, were rooms for the singers. One was beside the north gate and faced south. Another was beside the east gate and faced north.
He said to me, "The room facing south is for the priests who take care of the temple.
The room facing north is for the priests who take care of the altar. These are the descendants of Zadok, the only Levites who may come near the LORD to serve him."
Then he measured the inner courtyard. It was square, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide. The altar stood in front of the temple.

He brought me to the porch of the temple and measured the side pillars of the porch. They were five cubits thick on each side. The entrance was fourteen cubits wide, and its side walls were three cubits wide on each side.
The porch was twenty cubits wide and eleven cubits deep. Steps led up to it, and there were columns beside the side pillars, one on each side.
